_description: Part 14 - implementation-independent keyboard/accessibility BEHAVIOR contract (works whether the eventual UI is a modal, a command-palette overlay, or a dedicated page - see DESIGN FREEDOM in SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md). No visual design, no component names - this defines interaction behavior and ARIA semantics only, grounded in the real WAI-ARIA Combobox/Listbox pattern (the standard, well-established pattern for a search-with-live-suggestions input, not an invented one).
corePattern: WAI-ARIA 1.2 'Combobox with List Autocomplete' pattern (role=combobox on the input, aria-expanded reflecting whether results are showing, role=listbox on the results container, role=option on each result, aria-activedescendant on the input pointing at the currently-highlighted option's id) - this is the pattern real, production search-with-live-results UIs use (GitHub's own command palette, most site-search combobox implementations); not invented for this contract.

focusBehavior.onOpen: Focus moves to the search input immediately when the search surface opens (whatever triggers 'open' - see search-analytics-contract.json's site_search_open event, which should fire at this same moment).
focusBehavior.onClose: Focus returns to whatever element had focus before the search surface opened (the triggering element, e.g. a 'search' nav button) - never left on a now-hidden/removed element, and never reset to document.body. This is the single most commonly-missed a11y requirement for overlay/modal search UIs and is called out explicitly for that reason.
focusBehavior.trapping: If the eventual implementation is a modal/overlay (a DESIGN FREEDOM choice, not decided here), focus must stay within the search surface while open (standard modal focus-trap behavior) - if it's a dedicated page instead, no trapping is needed since there's no 'outside' to escape to.

keyboardBehavior.Tab: Moves focus forward through the search surface's own interactive elements in visual/logical order (input -> filter controls if visible -> nothing else, since results themselves are navigated by arrow keys, not Tab - per the combobox pattern, Tab should NOT move focus into the results list itself).
keyboardBehavior.ArrowDown: Moves aria-activedescendant to the next option in the results listbox (wrapping to the first result after the last, OR stopping at the last - either is an acceptable, real variant of the pattern; wrapping is the more common convention and is the default recommendation here). Does NOT move actual DOM focus off the input - the input keeps real focus throughout, only the 'active' visual/ARIA state moves, per the combobox pattern's own design (this is what lets the user keep typing while browsing results with arrows).
keyboardBehavior.Enter: Activates the currently-active-descendant result (same effect as clicking it) if one is active; if none is active (user hasn't arrowed to anything yet) and there is at least one result, activates the first (top-ranked) result - consistent with how a 'default choice' works in a combobox. Fires site_search_result_click either way.
keyboardBehavior.Escape: First press: clears the query text if non-empty (leaves the search surface open, matching common combobox convention of 'escape clears before it closes'). Second press (or first press if the query was already empty): closes the search surface entirely and returns focus per focusBehavior.onClose above. Fires site_search_close only on the closing press, not the clearing one.
keyboardBehavior.filterKeyboardAccess: Every facet control (whatever its final visual form) must be independently reachable and operable by keyboard alone (Tab to reach it, Enter/Space to toggle a value) - the same standard requirement as any other interactive control, called out explicitly because facet UIs are a common place this gets missed (e.g. a facet implemented as a non-focusable clickable div).

screenReaderAnnouncements.resultCount: An aria-live="polite" region (separate from the listbox itself, so it doesn't compete with option-by-option announcements) announces the result count after each settled query - e.g. '12 results' / '0 results' / '1 result' (singular/plural handled correctly) - sourced directly from search().results.length, the same real number result-count analytics already uses (site_search's own result_count parameter), not a separately-maintained string.
screenReaderAnnouncements.activeDescendant: As the user arrows through results, the currently-active option's own accessible name (its real title field - the same title every result already has, per the SearchDocument contract) is what a screen reader announces via the standard aria-activedescendant + role=option mechanism - no separate announcement text needs to be authored, the existing document title field already IS the accessible name.
screenReaderAnnouncements.emptyStateAnnouncement: Each of the 6 states in search-empty-states-contract.json needs a real, distinct announcement in the same aria-live region as resultCount above (not a second live region) - e.g. the noResults state announces '0 results for [normalized query]', the filteredNoResults state should distinguish itself ('0 results with current filters') per that file's own distinctFrom note, so a screen-reader user gets the same disambiguating information a sighted user would from a differently-worded empty state.
screenReaderAnnouncements.loadingAnnouncement: Only needed if a future implementation involves a real network round-trip with perceptible latency (e.g. the server-side search option discussed in search-performance-report.json) - a static-index client-side search resolves fast enough (see that file's own size/timing numbers) that a loading announcement would likely fire and clear faster than it could be perceived, which is itself a known anti-pattern (rapid-fire live-region churn). Contract: IF a loading state becomes perceptible (some real, measured threshold - commonly ~300-500ms is used as the point where a loading indicator becomes worth announcing), announce it in the same live region; if search stays instant given this corpus's real size, this is correctly omitted rather than added speculatively.

notDecided: Visual focus-ring styling, whether facet controls render as checkboxes/toggle-chips/a dropdown, exact announcement copy/wording (only that an announcement must exist and what data drives it), and color/contrast (a separate, standard WCAG concern the eventual visual design handles, not this data/behavior contract).
